_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the primary, market-neutral head term across all /es/ pages; it is the umbrella term for the whole product, not tied to one region.
phrases.good_example: Letras bonitas para copiar y pegar · Cursivas, aesthetic y símbolos para Instagram, TikTok y WhatsApp
phrases.avoid_when: n/a — this is the safe default term

phrases.content_surface: homepage FAQ answer, use-case card body copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Keep confined to body/FAQ/example text on the broad /es/ pages (as currently done) — do not promote to H1/title on the neutral homepage; safe as a dedicated term on an es_MX-specific spoke if one is ever built.
phrases.good_example: "Free Fire: en el nick del personaje. Aquí lo que más se usa son letras chidas, góticas, símbolos..." (es/index.html FAQ)
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use as the primary H1/title term on the broad, neutral /es/ homepage or hub pages — reserve for MX-specific contexts/examples.

phrases.content_surface: answer page H1/meta, FAQ items, guide body copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Primary term for the tofu-rendering answer page; safe to use as H1. Converges identically across all three markets — no regional variant needed.
phrases.good_example: "¿Por Qué Mi Nombre Sale Como Cuadros o Signos de Interrogación?" (es/answers/por-que-mi-nombre-sale-como-cuadros H1)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.english_concept: invisible character used to fake a blank name
phrases.content_surface: dedicated tool page title/H1, answer page
phrases.usage_guidance: Primary term for the invisible-character tool; converges across markets.
phrases.good_example: "Texto Invisible & Carácter Invisible" (es/texto-invisible H1); "usa la herramienta de copiar texto para copiar un espacio en blanco" (vidaextra.com, fetched)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Primary term for the 'how to' answer page; pair with the caveat that a 100% empty field is usually rejected (needs one filler char).
phrases.good_example: "Cómo Hacer un Nombre en Blanco (Invisible)" (es/answers/como-hacer-un-nombre-en-blanco H1)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Safe broad head term; converges across markets (also the exact phrasing used across multiple Taringa.net threads from ~15 years of LATAM forum history).
phrases.good_example: "Convierte tu texto en letras raras y símbolos Unicode únicos" (es/letras-raras hero-sub)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Keep 'aesthetic' untranslated — this matches universal practice across the whole Spanish-language web (Canva ES/MX, every competitor site); a Spanish calque ('estético') would read as wrong/awkward and was not found anywhere in the wild.
phrases.good_example: "¿Qué son las letras aesthetic y por qué se ven así?" (es/index.html FAQ)
phrases.avoid_when: Do not translate 'aesthetic' to 'estético/a' — not attested anywhere in native usage.

phrases.usage_guidance: Safe broad term; also confirmed used identically in MX-hosted editorial content (Canva ES/MX 'letras góticas' guide).
phrases.good_example: "Letras góticas para copiar y pegar" (es/letras-goticas title)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.native_phrase: nombre de usuario / nombre en pantalla
phrases.usage_guidance: This distinction is confirmed independently by mainstream Spanish tech editorial (unocero.com, infobae.com) using the same two terms — safe, correct, no regional variant.
phrases.good_example: "¿Dónde Funcionan las Fuentes Elegantes — Usuario o Nombre en Pantalla?" (es/answers/nombre-de-usuario-o-nombre-en-pantalla H1)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.native_phrase: por qué rechazaron mi nombre en el juego
phrases.english_concept: game rejected/wouldn't save the styled name
phrases.usage_guidance: Primary term for this answer page; confirmed by independent research that Free Fire's real error text is literally 'Nombre no válido' — consider surfacing that exact phrase since it's what users see and search for verbatim.
phrases.good_example: "¿Por Qué Rechazaron Mi Nombre en el Juego?" (es/answers/por-que-rechazaron-mi-nombre-en-el-juego H1)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.content_surface: FAQ item on the name-rejected answer page
phrases.usage_guidance: Correct, standard in-game economy term — use verbatim; pairs well with the checker-tool pitch ('validate before spending a card').
phrases.good_example: "¿Cómo evito desperdiciar una tarjeta de cambio de nombre?" (es/answers/por-que-rechazaron-mi-nombre-en-el-juego FAQ)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Use verbatim — matches the language Roblox's own validator/community uses.
phrases.good_example: "¿Por qué Roblox dice que mi nombre tiene caracteres no compatibles?" (es/answers/por-que-rechazaron-mi-nombre-en-el-juego FAQ)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Correctly distinguishes 'name genre/idea' (nombres aesthetic) from 'font style' (letras aesthetic, ES-007) — keep the distinction rather than merging the two pages.
phrases.good_example: "Nombres aesthetic ⋆｡˚ para copiar y pegar — Instagram, TikTok y juegos" (es/usecase/nombres-aesthetic title)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.native_phrase: letras para tatuajes / conversor de letras para tatuajes
phrases.usage_guidance: Matches real forum demand: Mediavida and Forocoches threads show people seeking font/style advice before a name tattoo; this term is the correct, natural way that demand is phrased.
phrases.good_example: "Conversor de letras para tatuajes" (es/usecase/letras-para-tatuajes H1)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: A confirmed, mainstream (dictionary-attested) Spain-register word for 'tacky' — usable in an 'avoid overdoing it' style-guidance callout (e.g. a tips FAQ on how many symbols is too many), but pair with a more neutral LATAM-safe synonym since it wasn't confirmed as equally natural outside Spain.
phrases.good_example: "Estamos alojados en un hotel cutre" (significadode.org, generic dictionary example, not text-styling specific)
phrases.avoid_when: Avoid as the sole word in LATAM-facing copy without a neutral pairing (e.g. 'recargado'/'sobrecargado', which forum evidence shows used more neutrally for 'too many symbols' complaints on elotrolado.net/Steam ES threads).

phrases.native_phrase: Feliz Día del Amor y la Amistad
phrases.content_surface: answer page FAQ body copy, alongside the neutral primary term
phrases.usage_guidance: This is a model example of correct regional handling per site policy: the page's title/H1 stays on the neutral 'San Valentín', while 'Feliz Día del Amor y la Amistad' is offered as one of the ready-to-use MX-flavored phrase options inside the body — exactly where a regional variant belongs.
phrases.good_example: "'Feliz San Valentín' sirve casi para cualquier persona... 'Feliz Día del Amor y la Amistad'" (es/answers/que-escribir-en-una-tarjeta-de-san-valentin FAQ)
phrases.avoid_when: Do not promote to the page H1/title — 'San Valentín' should stay primary since it's understood everywhere, MX included.

phrases.usage_guidance: The Spanish word itself is fine and correctly translated. The link target (/answers/, English) is NOT simply a wrong link to repoint, though: VERIFIED 2026-07-25 that /es/answers/index.html does not exist as a hub page (only 7 individual answer pages do) — repointing the nav href to /es/answers/ would 404. The real fix is building an /es/answers/ hub page first, then repointing the nav — a build, not a link correction. Same situation found for /tr/ (4 real answer pages, no hub, same header.js pattern).
phrases.good_example: n/a — this is a bug flag, not a usage example
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.native_phrase: nick único / nombre único y original
phrases.content_surface: not directly served by a dedicated page beyond nombres-aesthetic
phrases.usage_guidance: Real, recurring search formulation confirmed by both a fetched ForoBeta thread ('¿Ideas para crear un nick original?') and independent new search results describing 'buen nick' criteria (short, memorable, unique, easy to pronounce) — safe to use in an ideation-focused H2/FAQ.
phrases.good_example: "¿Para qué quieres un nick único? ¡Tú seguirás siendo la misma persona!" (ForoBeta, fetched)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.english_concept: character limit on a game/platform name field
phrases.content_surface: implicit in FAQ (caracteres cuentan como más de un carácter) but not a dedicated 'límite de caracteres' term
phrases.usage_guidance: Confirms and cross-checks the game-rules.js RULES table for Free Fire (limit: 12) against independent editorial sources — matches. Also surfaces that some styled symbols count as more than one character toward the limit, which the existing FAQ item ('¿Los caracteres elegantes cuentan como más de un carácter en el nombre de un juego?') already addresses correctly.
phrases.good_example: "tu nick puede tener hasta 12 caracteres y cada espacio invisible cuenta como uno" (vidaextra.com, fetched, on Free Fire)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.content_surface: homepage FAQ ('¿Cuál es la diferencia entre letras, fuentes y tipografía?')
phrases.usage_guidance: Confirmed as a distinct, correctly-scoped term from 'letras bonitas' by independent editorial sources (abcdario.org, letrasencursivas.com) explaining cursiva = the handwriting-style characteristic (slant, continuous stroke), while 'bonitas' is the broader decorative umbrella — the site's own FAQ answer already draws this distinction correctly.
phrases.good_example: "Letras es la palabra más usada en español... Fuente y tipografía se refieren más bien al diseño tipográfico" (es/index.html FAQ)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Correct, precise term for a genuinely Discord-specific mechanic (distinct from the general tofu/rejection problem) — good example of platform-specific depth beyond generic 'nombre rechazado' coverage.
phrases.good_example: "Un nombre de Discord con estilo puede fallar igualmente tres pruebas silenciosas: la lista de miembros, la @mención y el filtro de suplantación" (es/guide/nombre-discord-sin-riesgos meta description)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.content_surface: H1/meta of the letras-raras page; FAQ; style-card labels on nick-oriented pages
phrases.usage_guidance: Spanish splits this category by REGISTER, and the split is load-bearing: "letras bonitas" is the social/bio-facing term, "letras raras" is the gaming/nick-facing one. Use "raras" on nickname and game pages, "bonitas" on bio and social pages — do not swap them.
phrases.good_example: Letras Raras para Nick — Copiar y Pegar
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use "raras" on bio/aesthetic pages aimed at social profiles — there it reads as "odd-looking", which is not the compliment "bonitas" is.

phrases.english_concept: worksheet / activity sheet for a child
phrases.content_surface: h1, title, meta_description, faq, tool copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the noun for the generated sheet on any es_ES-facing printables page ('fichas de caligrafía para imprimir'). It supports the page's primary query target ('caligrafía para imprimir'), never replaces it. Do not use both 'ficha' and 'hoja de trabajo' in the same title.
phrases.good_example: Descarga las fichas de caligrafía para imprimir con el nombre de tu hijo.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use for es_MX copy — Mexican sites and teachers overwhelmingly say 'hojas de trabajo' or 'cuadernillo' (see P8). Do not use in technical/UI copy meaning a database record or a form field.

phrases.register: neutral, pedagogical but mainstream with parents
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the framing for a trazos/pre-writing section on an es printables page, and as an FAQ heading ('¿Qué es la grafomotricidad?'). Keep the H1 on the concrete deliverable ('fichas de trazos para imprimir'); grafomotricidad belongs in the supporting copy.
phrases.good_example: Fichas de trazos para trabajar la grafomotricidad de 3 a 5 años.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use on a page aimed at older children or at decorative/Unicode text — it is strictly an early-years handwriting-readiness term. Do not use it as the H1 head term; parents search the deliverable ('fichas de trazos'), and only then the concept.

phrases.english_concept: cursive/joined handwriting vs. block/print letters, as a school choice
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in FAQ/body on a Spanish cursive-printables page to disambiguate: state that the sheets generate 'letra ligada (cursiva)' and, if applicable, that block sheets are 'letra de imprenta'. This resolves the cursiva/italic ambiguity that plain 'cursiva' leaves open.
phrases.good_example: ¿Letra ligada o letra de imprenta? Nuestras fichas generan las dos.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'letra de imprenta' in es_MX copy — Mexico says 'letra de molde' (see P10). Do not use 'letra ligada' when the page is about italic *type* (that is 'cursiva' in the typographic sense) — mixing the two is the exact confusion this pair exists to prevent.

phrases.native_phrase: moldes de letras / letras grandes para imprimir
phrases.english_concept: large outline/bubble letters to print and colour
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the highest-value Spanish finding for the bubble-letters page: the natural query is 'moldes de letras para imprimir' / 'letras grandes para imprimir y colorear', not a literal translation of 'bubble letters'. Use it in H1/title; keep any 'letras burbuja' mention to a single supporting line at most.
phrases.good_example: Moldes de letras del abecedario para imprimir, colorear y recortar.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'moldes' when the output is on-screen Unicode text rather than a printable outline — 'molde' implies a physical template you cut or trace. Also avoid on pages about styling social-media text.

phrases.english_concept: repetition handwriting sheets ('write this line over and over')
phrases.usage_guidance: The single best es_MX head term for a handwriting-practice-sheet generator: 'planas de caligrafía para imprimir' names the exact artefact a Mexican parent has in mind. It supports, and does not compete with, a broader 'caligrafía para imprimir' target.
phrases.good_example: Genera planas de caligrafía con el nombre de tu hijo y descárgalas en PDF.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use in es_ES copy — in Spain 'plana' primarily reads as 'flat/page' and the drill is called a 'ficha de caligrafía'. Avoid where the tone is anti-rote: 'planas' carries a mild connotation of repetitive punishment-style homework for some Mexican adults, so do not use it in copy arguing that practice should be playful.

phrases.english_concept: lettering tattoo (the craft/category), as named by Spanish tattoo studios
phrases.register: studio-professional; also used by tattoo-curious customers who have read studio sites, but not a plain-consumer word
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'lettering' when describing the craft/style family on the Spanish tattoo page, alongside the consumer head term 'letras para tatuajes' (ES-014) which stays the H1. It reads as insider-correct rather than as an anglicism because that is genuinely how Spanish studios label the service.
phrases.good_example: Estilos de lettering: cursiva, gótica, Old English y chicano.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'lettering' as the page's primary title/H1 term — the searching consumer types 'letras para tatuajes'. Do not use it on non-tattoo pages (a bio/Instagram font page) where it carries no meaning for a general Spanish reader.

phrases.native_phrase: antes de llevarlo a la piel
phrases.english_concept: previewing lettering before committing — 'before it goes on the skin'
phrases.country_or_market: es_ES/es_LATAM (pan-Hispanic; market split not separable from the evidence)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the reassurance line near the generator ('mira tu nombre en cada estilo antes de llevarlo a la piel'). It supports the transactional intent of ES-014 without competing with the H1.
phrases.good_example: Prueba tu nombre en decenas de tipografías antes de llevarlo a la piel.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use on non-tattoo pages — 'la piel' only makes sense in a tattoo context. Do not use it to imply the output is a ready-to-ink stencil; pair it with the same caveat the DE page uses (the Unicode preview is a starting point, the artist draws the final lettering).

phrases.english_concept: the check/tick mark ✓ — Mexican everyday name
phrases.register: neutral everyday Mexican Spanish; safe in school, office and consumer copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Only for Mexico-targeted Spanish copy. On a pan-Spanish page, lead the H1 with the neutral 'marca de verificación ✓ / check' and name 'palomita' inside a body line ('en México se le llama palomita'), so the Mexican query is matched without asserting a Mexican name to Andean or Peninsular readers.
phrases.good_example: Copia la palomita ✓ y pégala en tu lista de pendientes.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use as the primary term in es_ES, es_AR, es_CO, es_VE, es_EC or es_PE copy — in the Andean markets the same symbol is 'chulo' or 'visto' (see P03), and 'palomita' there reads as either popcorn or a small dove. Do not use in technical/typographic documentation, where 'marca de verificación' is the expected term.

phrases.english_concept: the check/tick mark ✓ — Andean/Caribbean everyday name
phrases.register: neutral everyday; 'visto' is also fine in semi-formal/office copy, 'chulo' is more informal
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in market-targeted copy for those countries, or as the second name in a pan-Spanish body line that also mentions 'palomita' for Mexico. 'Visto' is the safer of the two for a shared-LATAM page because it carries the transparent 'reviewed/approved' meaning everywhere.
phrases.good_example: En Colombia a este símbolo ✓ se le dice chulo; en otros países, visto.
phrases.avoid_when: Never substitute 'chulo' into Mexican or Peninsular copy — in Spain 'chulo' primarily means cocky/flashy (and has a pimp sense), so it reads as an error or worse. Do not use either term in typographic/technical documentation, where 'marca de verificación' is expected.

phrases.english_concept: text-built face emoticon (kaomoji / text face) — the everyday browse word
phrases.register: casual, warm, mainstream; skews younger/female but not marked
phrases.content_surface: h1, title, category headings, tool copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Safe as the head noun on a Spanish kaomoji/text-faces page ('Caritas para copiar y pegar'). Pair it with the disambiguating qualifier the page actually targets — 'caritas con el teclado', 'caritas japonesas', 'caritas de texto' — because 'caritas' alone also returns graphical-emoji results. It supports, never replaces, the page's single primary query target.
phrases.good_example: Caritas para copiar y pegar — más de 500 emoticones hechos solo con caracteres.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use in technical/explanatory copy about Unicode codepoints, ASCII vs Unicode, or platform character limits — there 'caracteres' / 'emoticonos' is the correct register. Do not use it as the label for ASCII picture art (a cat drawn in characters is a 'dibujo', not a 'carita'). Evidence is Mexico/LatAm-weighted; do not assume it as the Spain-Spain head term without es_ES corroboration.

phrases.english_concept: kaomoji (upright Japanese-style text face) as a named category
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'emoticonos japoneses' as the plain-language head, and introduce 'kaomoji' once in the first paragraph as the proper name ('los kaomoji, o emoticonos japoneses'). That ordering matches how es.wikipedia and Spanish blogs actually write it and serves both queries without splitting the page.
phrases.good_example: Los kaomoji, o emoticonos japoneses, se leen derechos: no hace falta girar la cabeza.
phrases.avoid_when: Don't use it for Western sideways emoticons (:-)) — those are 'emoticonos occidentales'. Don't use it as a synonym for graphical emoji.

phrases.english_concept: ASCII art / picture drawn out of characters
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'arte ASCII' as the technical anchor (it matches the query 'arte ascii') and 'dibujos con caracteres' as the human-readable subheading/description. Category labels observed in the wild: Personas, Animales, Caras, Objetos, Gestos, Bailes, Texto, Estructuras, Decorativo — these are a ready-made, evidence-backed Spanish taxonomy for an ASCII-art collection page.
phrases.good_example: Más de 100 dibujos con caracteres para copiar: animales, caras, gestos y decorativos.
phrases.avoid_when: Don't use 'dibujos con caracteres' where the output is a single face emoticon — that's a 'carita'. Don't use it for a text-to-banner ASCII generator (that's 'texto en ASCII' / 'letras grandes'), which is a different job from a pre-made picture library.

phrases.english_concept: copypasta — a block of text (often ASCII/Unicode-heavy) spammed into chat
phrases.usage_guidance: Only relevant as a BOUNDARY: if a page offers big ASCII art or repeatable text blocks, an FAQ can note that mass-pasting them reads as a copypasta/spam and gets you muted. Never frame the tool as a copypasta generator.
phrases.good_example: Pegar el mismo dibujo muchas veces se considera copypasta y en la mayoría de servidores de Discord es motivo de silencio.
phrases.avoid_when: Never in a title, H1, meta, or CTA. Never as a positive framing of the product. Not appropriate in copy aimed at parents/teachers or in accessibility/technical explanations.

phrases.english_concept: modern calligraphy — the elegant hand-script style people want for invitations and cards
phrases.country_or_market: es_ES + es_LATAM (the term is used across both; no market-specific split found)
phrases.content_surface: faq, body copy, style-description text on a cursive/script page
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as a supporting descriptor on an existing cursive/script page to name the look the reader has in mind ('el efecto de la caligrafía moderna'). It must never replace the page's primary query target (letras cursivas / letras bonitas) — 'caligrafía moderna' is what the look is called, not what people type to find a copy-paste tool.
phrases.good_example: Si buscas el efecto de la caligrafía moderna —trazos finos al subir y gruesos al bajar— el estilo cursivo es el que más se le acerca.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages — this vocabulary belongs to a wedding/stationery audience and reads as off-register beside 'letras chidas' or 'nick'. Also avoid claiming the tool produces caligrafía: it produces Unicode glyphs, and the Spanish craft community draws a firm line between escribir (caligrafía) and a tipografía you download.

phrases.english_concept: 'font' in the formal/design register — the word this audience uses instead of the gaming-register 'letras'
phrases.content_surface: faq, body copy on formal-occasion sections; possible h2 on a cursive/script page
phrases.usage_guidance: Reach for 'tipografía' only when the surrounding sentence is about a printed/ceremonial piece. Elsewhere on the site keep 'letras' — swapping registers mid-page reads as machine-assembled copy. This word supports the existing primary target, never replaces it.
phrases.good_example: Para una invitación, la tipografía de los nombres puede ser muy trabajada siempre que el resto del texto sea sobrio.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages — a Free Fire player searching 'letras chidas' does not say 'tipografía', and using it there sounds like a design agency talking down to them. Also avoid where the page is really about Unicode characters, not typefaces: calling a Unicode style a 'tipografía' is technically wrong and a knowledgeable Spanish designer will notice.

phrases.usage_guidance: Prefer 'extracto' for findability; add 'Acerca de' as a parenthetical gloss so the copy matches whichever label the reader is looking at.
phrases.good_example: LinkedIn muestra solo las tres primeras líneas de tu extracto.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'extracto' for a non-LinkedIn bio. Do not assert which label LinkedIn currently shows without checking.

phrases.native_phrase: la ñ y las tildes se quedan normales
phrases.english_concept: diacritic non-conversion, Spanish — la ñ and the tildes stay plain
phrases.country_or_market: ES (evidence from a Spain-targeted site; not verified for MX/AR)
phrases.usage_guidance: Name la ñ explicitly in the ES FAQ heading rather than saying 'letras acentuadas' — the ñ is the case users care about and the one they search. Keep it as an expectation-setting answer, not an apology.
phrases.good_example: Unicode no tiene versión decorada de á, é, í, ó, ú ni ñ, así que esas letras se quedarán normales.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use for the empty-box failure (ES-003 / ES-025) or for a rejected name (ES-024). Not a title/H1 term.

phrases.native_phrase: no se ve igual en todos los dispositivos
phrases.english_concept: platform-dependent rendering — it doesn't look the same on every device / for every viewer
phrases.country_or_market: ES (evidence from a Spain-targeted site; not verified for LatAm)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the ES FAQ heading for the cross-device question and answer it with a concrete recommendation (test in the target app before saving the name) rather than a hedge. Spanish gaming copy already frames this as a competitive-play concern — that framing converts better than a generic compatibility note.
phrases.good_example: ¿Por qué algunos efectos no se ven igual en todos los dispositivos?
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use it as a disclaimer bolted onto a title or hero — it belongs in the FAQ, where it answers a question rather than seeding doubt at the top of the page. Not a title/H1 term.

phrases.native_phrase: nombre para clan con iniciales / nombres para clanes con la letra X
phrases.english_concept: clan name / clan tag built FROM the requester initials or a starting letter
phrases.content_surface: usecase page body / FAQ / an initials-seeded generator control label — NOT a title or H1 until demand is measured with an instrument
phrases.usage_guidance: This is how Spanish speakers actually ask for the job, and it is a different job from "tag de clan" (ES-021): they supply the letters and want names generated from them, rather than a tag restyled. If an initials-seeded feature is ever built, this is the phrasing to match in body copy.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use as a page title or H1 on demand evidence this qualitative — there is no volume figure behind it (Semrush unavailable 2026-08-01). Do not treat it as a synonym for "tag de clan"; the two describe different jobs.

phrases.content_surface: symbol identity page (if EN parent is ever built, per English-Parent Rule)
phrases.avoid_when: Do not conflate with Bolivia's boliviano or Venezuela's bolívar, which share a completely different (and separately confused) 'Bs.' abbreviation

phrases.english_concept: characters counted with or without spaces
phrases.usage_guidance: Use when explaining counting modes on the ES counter page; the ambiguity ('¿los 4000 caracteres son con espacios o sin espacios?') is the user's own framing.
phrases.avoid_when: in gaming/nickname copy — this is a forms/academic register

phrases.english_concept: invisible character (umbrella term for the whole invisible/blank-character concept family)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the primary umbrella term for the invisible-character concept family; 'espacio invisible' (ES-004) is the narrower inter-word-space case, 'nombre en blanco / nick invisible' (ES-005) is the naming-specific case — this is the general term tying them together.
phrases.good_example: Carácter Invisible (⠀): copia y pega

phrases.english_concept: personalized name-tracing sheet — the specific head term for a typed-name tracing product
phrases.content_surface: title/H1 for a name-tracing generator page
phrases.usage_guidance: More specific than ES-034's 'grafomotricidad / fichas de trazos' (generic pre-writing strokes) — this is the personalized, name-specific variant, and the one directly matching UTG's typed-name generator product.

phrases.content_surface: body copy / FAQ synonym coverage, not the primary title
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as an alternate/synonym in body copy or FAQ for MX-facing cursive-practice content, alongside 'letra cursiva' (ES-028) — do not replace the primary term, this is a regional variant to cover, not a better term.
phrases.avoid_when: Spain-facing copy (not confirmed in use there)

phrases.content_surface: not yet on any page — a candidate future printable format, not current copy
phrases.usage_guidance: A Mexican or Spanish reader would not recognize this word — do not use in neutral /es/ copy without a PE-specific gloss/example if this format is ever built.
phrases.avoid_when: non-Peruvian-facing copy
